title: "Bees 1: a honey bee colony from modules"
author: "Simon Frost"

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using MatrixCommunityModels
using Plots
```

This is the first of four vignettes that build a community of honey bees, *Varroa* mites,
deformed wing virus and bumblebees. Each step adds one thing, and each thing is a small,
named piece: a life-cycle net, a stage duration, a stratum, a response, or a pool. Nothing
is a hand-written simulation loop.

## A life cycle is a net

A honey bee worker is an egg for 3 days, a larva for 5 and a capped pupa for 12; she then
works in the hive and later forages. The life cycle is a `ValuedProjectionNet` from
CategoricalPopulationDynamics.jl: stages, and named transitions with a value each.

```{julia}
p = HONEYBEE_PARAMETERS
life = ValuedProjectionNet([:egg, :larva, :pupa, :hive, :forager],
    :hatching   => [(:egg => :larva) => p.egg_survival],
    :capping    => [(:larva => :pupa) => p.larva_survival],
    :emerging   => [(:pupa => :hive) => p.pupa_survival],
    :hive_life  => [(:hive => :hive) => 1 - p.hive_mortality],
    :recruiting => [(:hive => :forager) => 1 - p.hive_mortality],
    :foraging   => [(:forager => :forager) => 1.0])
to_matrix(life)
```

## Stage durations

`expand_stages` gives each brood stage its duration in days. The names stay readable, and
the old names remain usable as totals.

```{julia}
daily = expand_stages(ResponsiveProjectionNet(life), :egg => 3, :larva => 5, :pupa => 12;
                      ageing = Dict(:egg => p.egg_survival, :larva => p.larva_survival, :pupa => p.pupa_survival))
stage_names(daily)
```

```{julia}
transition_names(daily)
```

## Responses

The values above describe a bee in ideal conditions. What actually happens depends on the
colony and the season, and each dependence is a *response* attached to a named transition:
a function of a context `ctx` (the colony's own stages `ctx.n`, any shared pools
`ctx.pool`, and the day `ctx.env`) that scales the transition. For example, foragers die
faster on days when they can fly:

```{julia}
flying(ctx) = flight_index(day_of_year(ctx.env))
example = respond(daily, :foraging => ctx -> 1 - p.hive_mortality - p.forager_mortality * flying(ctx))
winter, summer = context(example, zeros(22), NamedTuple(), 15), context(example, zeros(22), NamedTuple(), 200)
to_matrix(example, winter)[22, 22], to_matrix(example, summer)[22, 22]
```

`honeybee()` attaches the full set, each taken from a published colony model:

| Transition | Response | Source |
|---|---|---|
| eggs laid (an inflow) | queen's seasonal laying rate, capped by the brood the adults can tend | HoPoMo; BEEHAVE |
| `larva_ageing` | larvae are lost when pollen or nurses are short | HoPoMo |
| `recruiting`, `hive_life` | hive bees become foragers, inhibited by foragers, faster when food is short; only on flying days while there is brood | Khoury et al. 2011, 2013 |
| `foraging` | extra mortality on flying days | Russell et al. 2013 |
| `hive_life`, `foraging` | starvation, and failure of very small colonies | Russell et al. 2013 |

The condition "while there is brood" is what produces winter bees: workers that emerge
after brood rearing has stopped are never recruited to foraging, and so live for months.

## Stores are another module

The colony's honey and pollen are two more entries of its state, with their own
transitions (`honey_kept`, `pollen_kept`: what is left after the day's consumption) and
inflows (what the foragers bring in). They are written as a separate net and merged into
the bees with `⊕`.

```{julia}
colony = honeybee()
stage_names(colony, :honeybee)[[1, 4, 9, 21, 22, 23, 24]]
```

```{julia}
transition_names(system(colony)[:honeybee])
```

## A year in the life of the colony

The time step is a day and the environment of each step is the day number. The colony
starts on 1 January with 10,000 workers and 25 kg of honey (the BEEHAVE default).

```{julia}
sol = project(colony, honeybee_state(colony), 1:(365 * 3))
days = sol.t ./ 365
adults = stage_total(sol, :honeybee, [:hive, :forager])
plot(days, [stage_total(sol, :honeybee, [:egg, :larva, :pupa]) stage_total(sol, :honeybee, :hive) stage_total(sol, :honeybee, :forager)];
     label = ["brood" "hive bees" "foragers"], xlabel = "Year", ylabel = "Bees", lw = 2)
```

```{julia}
second = 366:731
(peak_adults = round(Int, maximum(adults[second])), on_day = argmax(adults[second]),
 winter_cluster = round(Int, adults[731]),
 reared_per_year = round(Int, sum(stage_total(sol, :honeybee, :pupa12)[second])))
```

Published colonies peak at 40,000 to 60,000 adults in July, overwinter with roughly 10,000
and rear 120,000 to 150,000 workers a year (Seeley; Russell et al. 2013). The model's peak
is a little below that range; the other two are within it.

```{julia}
plot(days, [stage_total(sol, :honeybee, :honey) ./ 1000 stage_total(sol, :honeybee, :pollen) ./ 1000];
     label = ["honey (kg)" "pollen (kg)"], xlabel = "Year", ylabel = "Stores", lw = 2)
```

## Freezing the colony

On any day the colony is an ordinary matrix model. `frozen_net` returns it as a net with
that day's values, so each number can be traced to its transition.

```{julia}
june = 365 + 160
net = frozen_net(colony, :honeybee, sol.u[june + 1, :], june)
(recruiting = transition_matrix(net, :recruiting)[22, 21], foraging = transition_matrix(net, :foraging)[22, 22],
 hive_life = transition_matrix(net, :hive_life)[21, 21])
```

In June a hive bee has about a 4% chance per day of becoming a forager, and a forager
about a 10% chance per day of dying.

## What is provisional

The honey budget needed one adjustment to balance: 0.14 g of honey per nectar forager per
day, against 0.1 g per forager of any kind in Khoury et al. (2013) and Russell et al.
(2013). The share of foragers collecting pollen, and the use of brood as the cue for
recruitment, are modelling choices rather than published values. The climate behind
`flight_index` is illustrative. `HONEYBEE_PARAMETERS` and the comments in `src/bees.jl`
list every value with its source.
